images.note: Four-way race / election math beats. Contemporary: Alexander Hesler photograph, Springfield IL, June 3, 1860 (campaign season). SI copy is a gelatin silver print struck later from the 1860 negative; LOC copy is the 1860 carte-de-visite-era print. 1596x2000 alt.
images.title: Abraham Lincoln, Hesler portrait, June 1860

images.note: Four-way race beat: Northern Democratic nominee, popular sovereignty. Contemporary 1860 portraits. LOC primary is a Brady-era 1860 carte de visite (1250x2000).
images.title: Stephen A. Douglas, senator from Illinois, 1860

images.note: Four-way race beat: Southern Democratic nominee, sitting vice president, slavery in all the territories. LOC 1860 carte de visite contemporary (1314x2000); SI copy c.1861 (2000x3205).
images.title: John C. Breckinridge, 1860

images.note: Four-way race beat: Constitutional Union nominee, ex-Whig Tennessean, platform of the Union and silence on slavery. Contemporary: LOC 1859 Thirty-fifth Congress portrait (1537x2000); SI c.1859 (2000x2606).
images.title: John Bell, senator from Tennessee, 1859

images.note: Four-way race beat: the whole field in one frame. Contemporary 1860 campaign cartoons. Primary: Currier & Ives 'The National Game' lithograph (baseball game with Lincoln, Douglas, Breckinridge, Bell). Alt: 'The rail candidate' lithograph, Lincoln straddling a rail (rail-splitter / antislavery-plank pun).
images.title: The National Game, Currier & Ives campaign cartoon, 1860

images.note: Election-math beat: 'the map was the whole election,' 18 free vs 15 slave states, free states already hold the electoral majority. Contemporary: 1861 map compiled from the 1860 census showing slave-population distribution across the southern states (2000x1595). No second qualifying institutional image found; Lloyd's 1861 chart (u5l6-lloyds-chart) is the companion piece.
images.source: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
images.title: Map of slave-population distribution, compiled from the 1860 census, 1861

images.note: Election-math / secession-winter beat: 1861 broadside chart with a U.S. map coloring free states, border states, cotton states, and territories differently, plus portraits of Lincoln and his cabinet. Contemporary (1554x2000). Same-institution companion to u5l6-section-map, so no alt_url; no second qualifying institution found.
images.title: Lloyd's new political chart, 1861

images.note: Four-way race beat: the Charleston split. Contemporary 1860 engraving of the Southern seceders' meeting at St. Andrew's Hall after walking out of the Democratic convention (2000x1540). No second qualifying institutional image: the Smithsonian NMAH engraving of the Charleston convention has no digital image online.
images.title: Meeting of the Southern seceders from the Democratic Convention, Charleston, 1860

images.note: Secession-winter context beat: John Brown's October 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry and Northern sympathy for him. Contemporary 1859 photographs (LOC 1654x2000; NPG 2000x2680).
images.title: John Brown, portrait, 1859

images.note: Secession-winter context beat: 'Colonel Robert E. Lee led the Marines that captured him.' Contemporary 1859 wood engraving of U.S. Marines storming the engine house (2000x1615). No second qualifying institutional image found at the bar.
images.title: U.S. Marines storming the engine house, Harpers Ferry, 1859

images.note: Harpers Ferry beat: Lee commanded the Marines that captured Brown. Primary is contemporary: 'Gen. Robert E. Lee,' 1860 (2000x1476). Alt is LATER: Mathew Brady photograph, 1864 (2000x3015) - wartime likeness, not 1859-60 appearance; use primary for period accuracy.
images.title: Gen. Robert E. Lee, 1860

images.note: Secession-winter beat: South Carolina, December 20, 1860, first out. Primary: contemporary 1860 print of the 'The Union is Dissolved!' Charleston broadside (2000x3896). Alt: contemporary 1860 Frank Leslie's engraving of the Charleston mass meeting endorsing the legislature's call for a secession convention (2000x1484).
images.title: 'The Union is Dissolved!' broadside print, Charleston, December 20, 1860

images.note: Secession-winter beat: the seceders name slavery themselves. Contemporary 1861 pamphlet 'An address setting forth the declaration of the immediate causes which induce and justify the secession of Mississippi from the Federal Union' (Jackson: Mississippian Book and Job Printing Office, 1861) - this scan page shows the title and the 'Our position is thoroughly identified with the institution of slavery' passage quoted in the script (2303x3857). Scan by Internet Archive with Duke University Libraries funding; the Mississippi Department of Archives and History holds the pamphlet but serves it as PDF only (no qualifying image). No second qualifying institutional image.
images.source: Internet Archive (Duke University Libraries scan of the 1861 pamphlet)
images.title: Mississippi Declaration of the Immediate Causes, 1861 pamphlet page

images.note: Secession-winter beat: elected president of the Confederate States at Montgomery, February 1861. Contemporary portraits: LOC 1861 three-quarter-length (1599x2000); NPG c.1861 (2000x2754).
images.title: Jefferson Davis, 1861

images.note: Secession-winter beat: the Cornerstone Speech (March 21, 1861, Savannah). Contemporary portraits: LOC 1860 half-length studio portrait (1218x2000); NPG c.1860 (2000x2967).
images.title: Alexander H. Stephens, 1860

images.note: Secession-winter beat: Montgomery, Alabama, February 1861 - CSA formed, Davis elected. LATER depictions (honest): primary is an 1878 engraving of Davis's inauguration at the Alabama State Capitol, February 18, 1861 (1999x2689); alt is an 1878 chromolithograph of the crowd at the capitol for the announcement of Davis as president (1527x2000). No contemporary 1861 inauguration image found at the bar; the NPG 1861 Whitehurst & Hinton cabinet photograph exists but shows the cabinet, not the event.
images.title: Inauguration of Jefferson Davis, Montgomery, February 18, 1861 (1878 engraving)

images.note: Secession-winter beat: the Crittenden Compromise rescue attempt. Contemporary portraits of Senator John J. Crittenden of Kentucky: LOC 1859 Thirty-fifth Congress (1576x2000); NPG c.1860-63 (1999x2645).
images.title: John J. Crittenden, senator from Kentucky, 1859

images.note: Secession-winter beat: Buchanan's December 1860 message - secession illegal, but no federal power to coerce. Contemporary portraits: LOC 1857, fifteenth president (1433x2000); NPG c.1860 (2000x2575).
images.title: James Buchanan, fifteenth president, 1857

images.alt_source: Metropolitan Museum of Art (via Internet Archive)
images.note: Fort Sumter beat: April 12, 1861, Confederate guns open; the fort surrenders after the bombardment. Contemporary 1861 photograph of Fort Sumter after the first bombardment (2000x1042). No second qualifying institutional image: SI/NMAH Sumter records have no digital images; the Met's George S. Cook holdings were unreachable (collection API down).
images.title: Fort Sumter after the first bombardment, 1861
